data.name: Ghost Ship (Gather)
data.description: The legendary Ghost Ship has returned, a warship thought destroyed decades ago now hanging over the coast on a lattice of impossible seals. Board it before it vanishes, learn what the Skyglass Core preserved, and escape with whatever the lost project still guards.
data.successDescription: The Ghost Ship fades from the sky as suddenly as it came. What you recovered is real. So are the signs that something aboard still remembers the old mission.

objectives.description: The Ghost Ship appears without approach. One moment the moon is clear; the next, a black hull hangs beneath it, seal-light burning through the keel where the sea should be. Every record says the vessel was destroyed decades ago. Tonight it lowers a gangplank.
At the top of the gangplank, the Deck Warden takes shape from pale script and old armor. Behind him, two seal charges hum beside the rail. His face is young. The uniform is generations out of date.
Break the Deck Warden and the unstable charges guarding the entry.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The Deck Warden drives you back over the rail. The ship does not pursue. Board again.
Climb the anchor chain beneath the hull. The metal is warm with chakra, and every few breaths the ship seems to lose weight beneath your hands.

Inside the lower hull, cracked seal-lines leak pale chakra into soaked timber and cable. The wreckage gathers itself around a half-formed human outline, as if the ship remembers a crew member badly. The Core Horror turns toward you.
The Core Horror tears itself free of the lower hull.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The Horror collapses over you in timber, cable, and cold chakra. When the ship rebuilds the breach, you are back outside it. Climb again.

The Oathkeeper appears at the rail in an officer's coat faded by no weather. Pale seal-script passes through his hands. 'Answer true and walk aboard oathbound. Answer false and prove yourself by force. What does every traveler keep while every journey spends it?'
'Time.' For the first time, the Oathkeeper smiles. 'We had plenty of that.' He steps aside as seal-lines brighten beneath your feet. 'Oath accepted. The Captain will know.'

nextObjectiveId.text: Ask what the oath still means

objectives.description: 'Wrong.' The Oathkeeper draws a narrow blade and salutes. 'Then show me what the living learned while we were gone.'
The Oathkeeper lowers his blade and begins the test.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The Oathkeeper's blade finds you three times. He lowers it, unimpressed, and the ship's seals cast you back outside. Call again.

The deck is too wide for the hull beneath it. Empty mess tables are laid for a meal no one has touched, while crew afterimages repeat their stations between pulses of seal-light. Three routes open ahead: the chart room, the sealed hold, or the long walk to the helm.

The Wayfinder looks up from charts layered with decades of corrections. Some mark villages that did not exist when his uniform was new. Others show mountains from angles no ground navigator could have drawn. 'Still no home port,' he says.
The Wayfinder redraws the room around you.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: Ink, seal-light, and false horizons swallow the room. When your sight returns, you are back on the deck. The chart room waits.
Among the impossible routes is an old field cache, marked before the ship vanished. The ink is decades old. The Wayfinder's newest corrections are not.

nextObjectiveId.text: Compare the old and new charts

objectives.description: Rows of sealed crates fill the hold. Inventory slates show the same quantities checked again and again across decades. The Arsenal Keeper stands among untouched rations and medicine. 'Nothing leaves unaccounted.'
The Arsenal Keeper raises the counterweight maul.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The maul ends the argument. The ship's seals cast you back to the deck while the hold closes behind him. Descend again.
Two Deck Wardens hold the approach to the helm. Beyond them, the command dais glows around a fractured ring of white crystal.
The Wardens bar the last steps to the helm.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The Wardens hold the passage and the command dais remains beyond them. Try again.
Even the oathbound are tested before the helm. Two Deck Wardens step into the passage as the seal-lines beneath them flare white.
The Wardens bar the way, oath or no oath.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The Wardens hold. The oath remains recorded. Try the passage again.
A notation along the route sheet reads: 'Where the cliff drinks and the stone keeps watch, the cache sleeps beneath the watcher's shadow.' Three coves match part of the description.

nextObjectiveId.text: The cove beneath the stone shrine
The cove with the split cliff
The open beach past the reef

objectives.description: You dig until the tide reaches your knees. Broken seal plates and driftwood, nothing more. The watcher's shadow falls elsewhere.
Only reef stone and an old anchor frame lie beneath the sand. Re-read the route sheet.
Dig beneath the stone watcher's shadow before the tide shifts.
Your shovel strikes metal. Sand bursts outward as the Guardian unfolds from a buried seal frame, armor plated with shell and stone around the cache.
The Guardian rises between you and the cache.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The Guardian drives you into the sand and settles back over the buried seal frame. The cache remains.
The Guardian breaks apart into sand and fading script. Beneath it sits a sealed field cache stamped with the same Skyglass project mark etched into the ship's keel.
You recover a field cache left before the Ghost Ship vanished. Its supplies are old. The seal keeping them preserved is still active.
Unsealed supplies can be carried out now. Behind them, a black reinforcement door bears the Captain's personal seal. Nothing in the hold looks used, only counted.
You shoulder a supply crate and head for the rail. The Deck Warden reforms in the exit path, chakra hook already in hand.
The Deck Warden bars the exit one last time.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The Warden catches you before the rail and drags the crate back into the hold. The exit remains.
You reach the shore with the crate as the Ghost Ship begins to lift away. The haul is modest, but real.
You chose the sure supplies and escaped before the ship vanished again.

The Captain's seal breaks. Cold wind spills from a room without windows. The First Blade steps out in the uniform of a dead era, twin cleavers forming from the gale. 'Finally,' he says. 'Something new.'

nextObjectiveId.text: Ask how long he has waited

objectives.description: The First Blade steps through the broken seal.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The gale folds the room around you. When the ship releases you, the Captain's seal is whole again. Break it once more.
The wind dies with the First Blade. The restricted vault stands open, revealing equipment the crew itself was never meant to touch.

nextObjectiveId.text: Listen to the First Blade's final words

objectives.description: You broke the Captain's private seal and claimed what the ship had guarded from its own crew.

At the command dais stands the Captain, almost solid beneath the core-link seals. An empty ring of white crystal hangs above him. 'They built this ship to cross any wall and outlast any siege,' he says. 'No one asked what outlasting everything would cost.'
The Captain steps down from the command dais.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The Captain ends the duel and the helm flashes white. A moment later you are back at the approach, the challenge still waiting.
The Captain lowers his weapon. 'The ship died once. Skyglass disagreed.' Behind him, the command stores unlock.
You cross the Ghost Ship from rail to helm and defeat the Captain it remembers. The command stores open, but the ship itself shows no sign of ending.

The Captain turns before you reach the dais. The Oathkeeper's mark burns across the floor. White crystal rises from the control ring and closes around his brow. 'The order was preserve command, preserve crew, keep the vessel airborne until the mission ended. The mission never ended.'
The Skyglass Crown completes itself. Every seal on the Ghost Ship answers at once as the Crowned Captain steps down.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The Crowned Captain breaks your guard and the helm flashes white. The oath remains recorded. When you return to the dais, he is waiting at full synchronization.

White crystal fractures from his brow and hangs in the air as fading shards. The Captain drops to one knee. 'Now you understand why they feared us.' The command stores open behind him as the ship begins to fade.
You defeat the Ghost Ship's most complete memory of its Captain. The vessel slips out of the world again, still following a mission no living shinobi remembers.
The Deck Warden falls apart in a brief spray of pale script. Before the last seal-light fades, another outline begins forming at the watch post. The ship has not lost its guard. It has restarted him.
Below your boots, cloud banks move through the open night. The hull hangs above the coast on iron bracing and pale lift seals. One channel leaks through a damaged seam leading into the lower hull.

The upward seal channels hold the ship aloft. A thinner line runs against their flow, carrying fragments of handwriting and fractured memories toward a sealed section inside the hull. Someone once tried to isolate a failure from the main network.

nextObjectiveId.text: Follow the breach into the hull

objectives.description: With the Core Horror defeated, the surrounding frame begins sketching its ruined body again. A ladder rises to the deck. Beneath it, a severed impression conduit pulses toward a sealed maintenance chamber.

Rows of framed seal patterns stand without occupants. Each carries a human impression, not a living body: a remembered greeting, the shape of a hand reaching for warm tea, a command repeated until its meaning has faded. A small maintenance plate is locked behind the frames.

Three seal paths remain on the plate. One rises to the lift network, one bears the Captain's command mark, and a third turns back beneath the inactive frames. Beside the return path someone scratched: 'What command cannot repair must first be quarantined.'

nextObjectiveId.text: Trace the return seal beneath the frames

objectives.description: The chosen channel rejects the intrusion. Iron shutters seal the maintenance plate, and the impression frames fall quiet. The quarantine passage is no longer reachable on this visit, but the ladder to the deck remains open.

The returning seal opens a narrow chamber not marked on any ship plan. Command records and damaged crew impressions were moved here and filed as containment faults. A black iron Reliquary is chained to the far wall. Its custodian has not yet appeared.

The reports span decades. Each warns that reconstructed patterns are deteriorating while preservation remains mandatory. The same seal-engineer's signature appears on every revision, although no living engineer could have filed them all. The final correction is stamped 'Access refused by command priority.'

A senior shinobi engineer gathers from the engraved lines, his form steadier than the damaged crew below. 'I sealed the worst of it away,' the Sealwright says. 'Command would not permit me to stop the work. It will not permit you to take these records.' He raises a sealing stance before the Reliquary.
Break the Sealwright's containment defense.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw

objectives.description: The seals close around you and force you back before the Reliquary. The Sealwright resumes his watch.

The Sealwright's reconstructed body unthreads into orderly strands of chakra. The containment case unlatches. Inside sits a preserved Skyglass Reliquary, untouched by the ship's repeating stores inventory. Taking it will end this expedition; the Captain and ordinary rewards lie elsewhere.

nextObjectiveId.text: Recover the Reliquary and leave the ship

objectives.description: You escape with the Skyglass Reliquary and the evidence of a hidden containment failure. Above the coast, the warship continues its course. You have taken a piece of its history, not ended its mission.

Under the first route lies a map of places that did not yet exist when the ship vanished. The Wayfinder corrected the same journey again and again as villages moved, roads changed, and generations passed. The marked shore cache is real, but the final clue must be read against the newest chart.
You dig where the split cliff breaks the tide. Beneath the sand you find old seal fragments, but the shadow of the stone watcher never reaches this cove.
The open beach yields only an abandoned anchor brace and reef stone. This cove has no watching shrine and no shadow to measure.

After the Arsenal Keeper falls, the inventory slate keeps counting. Medicine is still sealed, provisions are untouched, and every audit carries a fresh entry in the same officer's hand. The restricted vault remains locked behind the racks.

The Arsenal Keeper recorded the same request for shore leave on successive inventories, each time crossing it out with the words 'crew not relieved.' The ship remembered hunger and rest. Its reconstructed crew could enjoy neither.

The First Blade lowers his swords a fraction. 'Every watch begins where the last one ended,' he says. 'I know each strike before it comes. Yours are the first footsteps I have not practiced.' His grin is genuine as he raises his blades again.

nextObjectiveId.text: Give him the duel he wants

objectives.description: The First Blade's fading impression leaves one sentence behind: 'That was new.' The vault begins repairing its broken seals as you depart with the restricted stores.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the sealed stores and depart

objectives.description: Beyond the defeated helm guard, a viewing gallery overlooks the command seal network. The Captain waits on the dais ahead. The gallery offers a closer look at the systems that kept the Ghost Ship airborne through its destruction.

Seal diagrams show navigation, defensive lines, and crew reconstruction drawing from one command interface. A preserved damage report marks the original hull loss as incomplete, while the final command acknowledgement remains locked behind the Crown's authority.

With the ordinary Captain defeated, the command network still hums. The loss was never accepted as final. A deeper order remains beyond the access of this incomplete command imprint, and the ship is already beginning to correct the damage of battle.

The Crown's restored command memory leaves a final recorded order: preserve command, preserve crew, maintain flight until the mission ends. There is no termination acknowledgement. Even without its Captain standing, the Core begins reconstructing the helm. The record offers proof, not control.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the oathbound reward and depart

objectives.description: The Oathkeeper traces the old access oath across his glove. 'I know that I died,' he says, 'but not how to finish this watch. The Captain's crown remembers what the rest of us cannot.' He opens the command passage without asking for another answer.
